notes: Per-harness progress watchdog in tools/runner, mirroring T634's shape. THE DEFECT: T214's progress watchdog fired at a flat --progress-timeout 600 s with no [progress] line — the identical defect T634 fixed in the STARTUP fuse for claude, left un-fixed in the PROGRESS fuse for pi/ollama. A deepseek lane does normal long work (p95 wall 2445.05 s, n=66) and its stream goes quiet during long reasoning stretches while it writes its deliverable, so 600 s killed finished lanes: T526 (deepseek-v4-flash, 1129.6 s, 870 uncommitted lines), T635 (deepseek-v4-pro, 1732.6 s, no artifact), T638 (deepseek-v4-flash, 1901.3 s, COMPLETE — 25/25 verdicts written). All three walls are BELOW the family p95, so the fuse was catching normal work, not stalls. THE FIX, two halves mirroring T634: (1) the progress sensor for pi/ollama adds the declared deliverables' mtime to the existing stdout/stderr/[progress] signal — a lane writing its deliverable is making progress, whatever its stream says; (2) the threshold is derived, not chosen: 3 x observed p95 wall per family, computed from untracked/runs/*.json (finalized non-killed runs, excluding the T542 bakeoff gate sub-runs, classified by child binary, p95 by linear interpolation): pi/deepseek 2445.05 s n=66 -> 7336 s (ceil of 7335.15); ollama 2255.02 s n=9 -> 6766 s (ceil of 6765.06). New flag --agent-progress-timeout (None=derive, 0=disable, positive=override). DISAGREEMENT WITH T634, stated: T634 reported deepseek p95 2340.9 s (n=113); my snapshot is 2445.05 s (n=66). The denominators differ because (a) T634's n=113 counted the 55 T542 bakeoff gate sub-runs (wall 0.0-0.6 s, a different harness shape) which drag the p95 down, and (b) 10 more deepseek runs landed since T634's snapshot; the archive swept 30 records on 2026-08-20. Excluding bakeoff sub-runs is the conservative direction (higher threshold, fewer false kills) and is required by '>= 3x p95'. KILLS ARE UNSCOREABLE: the reason still starts 'progress timeout', which the runner's _killed_by maps to 'watchdog' (T629's vocabulary — no second enum); every scorer refuses killed_by != none (Ruling 32). RE-KEY: T526 (deepseek-v4-flash) was already re-keyed killed_by=watchdog by T629 (its record was overwritten by the later pro re-dispatch; the kill is proven by untracked/log/t526.log '[runner] KILL: progress timeout 600s' at wall 1129.6 s); T635 (deepseek-v4-pro, model-perf.md line 88) re-keyed killed_by=watchdog — evidence untracked/log/t635.log '[runner] KILL: progress timeout 600s' + exit 124 in 1732.6 s (its run record is launch-only: overwritten by a later re-dispatch); T638 (deepseek-v4-flash, line 89) re-keyed killed_by=watchdog — its run record carries killed='progress timeout 600s' signal 9 wall 1901.3 s. EARLIER-ROW REPORT: no OTHER row in docs/infra/model-perf.md is a progress-watchdog kill misattributed as a model failure — the only 'progress timeout' kills on disk or in untracked/log are T526/T635/T638 (plus two runner/<pid>-named T214 regression fixtures in the archive, not worker lanes). The un-keyed fail rows (T530 wall x2, T573 wall, T591 rc=-15, T599/T603/T604/T606/T607) are wall/SIGTERM/provider kills, NOT progress-watchdog kills, so they are T630's scope, not T643's. MARGINS under the new threshold (7336 s vs 600 s): T526 +6736 s of quiet time, T635 +6736 s, T638 +6736 s; additionally T638 (25/25 verdicts = findings/T638-race-g.json, a declared deliverable) and T526 (declared deliverables tools/bakeoff.sh + regression + findings) are kept alive CONTINUOUSLY by the new deliverable-mtime sensor while they write, so the threshold is not even reached. CONTROLS (test-first, red then green): RED against HEAD tools/runner replaying T638's shape (pi-named stub emits one liveness line then writes deliverable.txt every 1 s for 5 s, no [progress], --progress-timeout 3) -> '[runner] KILL: progress timeout 3s (3s) — no [progress] for 3s' exit 124 in 5.3 s with all 5 deliverable lines written — the exact T638 shape. GREEN against the fixed runner (same fixture, --agent-progress-timeout 4) -> exit 0, 5 verdicts on disk. Seeded stall arm (emits once, then no output + no mtime) still killed exit 124 killed_by=watchdog; null arms: T586 startup fuse unchanged, T214 non-agent [progress] watchdog unchanged, per-family derived thresholds printed (pi 7336 s, ollama 6766 s). Regression wired into zig build test (build.zig). All pre-existing runner regressions stay green (startup-liveness, claude-liveness, guard, reporting, taskid, brief-telemetry, reap, worktree). Landmark: advances L1 (measurement integrity) — the fuse no longer writes false model-failure rows for the streaming harness's normal long work. Full evidence + red/green quotes in findings/T643-context.json.
